"What does this mean?"

The first person has the key.  They may be scared because it doesn't fit any lock in their house.  Then, the second person has the key too.  The two people can come together and open a new door, and see what happens on the other side.  This new door can lead to a new adventure.  They can start a whole new story with the key.

In this story, there are two main characters.  They work together to solve a problem and find an answer.  The characters start out confused and scared.  They also change because they were able to come up with an answer to a problem.  This story has a moral of problem solving and using teamwork to overcome problems.

A good title for the story could be "The Key that Didn't Fit Any Lock."

(From the film's script) 

Narrator: The man found a key that did not fit in his house.
His wife went crazy.
They ended up in court.
And you can tell the judge just what you think.

The judge says,
 “You can tell him just what you think”
and that’s a key that doesn’t fit any lock.


The narrator explains the key that doesn't fit any lock has been found, then shows us why this happens. It's a very quick story with no dialogue or action, just dialogue. I suspect there is a lesson here about getting what you want.

My father had always believed that if he ever found a key that didn't fit any locks in the house he should put it on a chain and wear it to identify himself.  My mother was always afraid that he would do that and embarrass her.
We lived in a rather small house in a small town, and my parents were typical in that they had little privacy.  Their bedroom was between the living room and the kitchen, and as my father was one of those people who always had to make noise and make it heard, my mother would often get up and leave the bedroom and lock the door.  Then she would listen to the news.  My parents had separate radio's.  My father's radio was a large old black radio that sat on a night table.  It was often so loud that she would have to keep the door locked just so she could hear the news.  When she turned on the radio, my father could tell because he could hear it through the bathroom.  It was the little things that counted.  Often he would do it on purpose.

When I began writing this story, I wasn't sure where it would go. I imagined a woman who finds a key that doesn't fit in her home's locks and decides to put it somewhere safe, thinking she might need it in the future. Her actions set the key in motion, with no way to know how it will be used or by whom. The key is a symbolic object; it can unlock anything but has no purpose beyond that. I think it is important to always have hope that things will be better, even if you don't know how they'll get there.

John was the kind of man who couldn't stand being stuck with someone or something else's trash. His wife's clothes never seemed to fit right, he couldn't get away with a child's smile for very long, and every door and cupboard in their home seemed to contain only someone else's stuff.

It was a problem that had only been made worse by a recent move. When John and Mary had bought their new house, they'd spent years moving in. The problem was, that the new owners were very messy people, and had left an incredible amount of clutter behind.

After several months of packing boxes, carrying things, and opening things that the new owners never seemed to care about, John had started to develop a few ticks. He was constantly looking around the house, checking each room, the attic and the basement for some of the previous owner's belongings that he could throw out.

Tonight, it seemed like a miracle had happened. As John was heading upstairs, he felt something in his pocket. Upon reaching the top, he pulled it out. It was a small, brass key.
It's important to take the time to do things right.

A couple were getting ready for bed when they found a set of keys on the floor. They searched their room and entire house but couldn't find the key that the new set would go with.

That afternoon their daughter arrived home from college to get ready for the big move back to the dorm. After unpacking her things she went out to grab some lunch.

When she returned there were no keys on the table to the new apartment.

She ran around the yard and found the key under the bushes.

When she opened the door, the couple was sitting on the couch enjoying the television.

The daughter ran over to them in tears.

"You gave me the wrong set of keys," she wailed.

A month later they moved out. The daughter and her husband are moving in this weekend.

The key turned in the lock and the door slowly opened. The room was dark but it was still enough to see the black cloak. He entered the room and slowly walked towards the table. There was another man sitting there staring at him. He held the key in his hand and slowly pulled it out.

He looked at the man and asked "Why do we do this? Why don't we just let go of this game and start fresh?"

The other man smiled and replied "Oh, you know why. You need to find the key. You've always wanted to go out and play. Now it's your time." He threw the key on the table and pulled out his own key and slowly put it into the keyhole. The door opened as the key was fully in. The other man walked out into the hallway and disappeared.

It's your turn now. Take the key and follow me, we've got to find the way out of here.

This one is pretty straightforward, but there are plenty of possibilities. For example, you could have a story in which the lighthouse keeper reads the letter and then does something because of the letter. Perhaps it was just a mistake and the letter was meant for him, but he still decides to do something that he otherwise might not have done because of that letter. Or you could have a story in which the lighthouse keeper reads the letter and then goes crazy because he doesn't know what to do with it, or he's afraid of what it might mean if it was actually addressed to the lighthouse and the person who wrote it isn't there anymore. Or you could have a story in which the lighthouse keeper receives the letter and is excited to open it, but then realizes it's only a boring catalog or something and he has no idea who it came from or why. In all of these cases, the lighthouse itself is going to be an important character in the story because it's the one thing that's actually there for the lighthouse keeper to interact with.

It makes for an interesting short story. As a story on its own, it could be fantastic. But as a writing practice, the story is flat.

Some translators who work on these words are tempted to bring them into the second language anyway, to try to find room where room shouldn’t be. The edges of languages are dangerous. There are many ways of being lost and found. We do not choose our way. We are chosen. The only question is this: what is the language that calls to us?

This isn’t much of a story at all, but more a meditation on how the loss of bells as a familiar and comforting background can have profound and lasting effects on a person. 

I started by picking the title as if it were the title of a poem or novel, a reference to the poem “The Horses” by Allen Ginsberg. The poem imagines a post-apocalyptic future where all industrial life ceases but in which all forms of animal life are spared. The narrator witnesses the return of horses which eventually gather in a field and are transformed into a “new beginning”. The bells I imagined as a symbol of this “old beginning” would be an ancient and universal sound that would continue to be heard in a world devoid of factories and machinery. 

The line about the “city's bells stop ringing the first morning” is borrowed from an opening line from the opening of the novel, “The Bell Jar” by Sylvia Plath. In the novel, the narrator describes the sound of the city's bells ringing in the morning when she awakes.

Bells ring. What do the bells ring?

In the old city streets, when the sun comes up the bell at the monastery rings to say morning prayers to God. Then the bell in the tower of the great clock rings to call the people out of their homes to begin the business of the day. The bell in the bell tower of the cathedral rings to celebrate the rising of the sun and the glory of its God. The bells all throughout the city ring as well in celebration of life.

When the bells of a city stop ringing, they do not ring because the sun has come up. They do not ring because the morning prayers are over. The do not ring because the hours of work have ended. And they do not ring because the glory of God, the glory of life, the glory of love, have ceased. The bells of a city do not ring because the city has died.
